official.deadline_note: Most country/territory pages published 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC; a small number of country pages list 20 October 2026. The exact deadline lives on your own country/territory page and the application system closes after it.
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 cycle; studies begin in the UK in September/October 2027
official.status_note: Official country page states 'Applications for 2027-2028 Chevening Scholarships are now closed' (verified 10 October 2026); participating SIDS country pages show the same closed status.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official FAQ: award recipients receive 'Payment of tuition fees'. Course guidance adds: an MBA fee cap of £22,000 applies (the scholar covers any excess over the cap); some universities require a tuition fee deposit that Chevening will not pay; most UK universities contribute 20% towards tuition fees for Chevening scholars.
benefits: A monthly personal living allowance (stipend) to cover accommodation and living expenses; the rate depends on studying inside or outside London and is subject to annual review
Economy travel to and from your country of residence by an approved route for you only
The cost of an entry clearance (visa) application for you only
An arrival allowance and a departure allowance
A travel top up allowance and a contribution of up to £75 for TB testing, where this is required
SIDS scholars additionally receive an enhanced UK programme of exclusive events and exclusive networking opportunities, plus access to the global alumni community
eligibility: To be eligible for a Chevening SIDS Scholarship you must meet the standard eligibility criteria for Chevening and be a citizen from one of the participating countries shown on the map on the SIDS page
Be a citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory; if applying from an ODA-eligible country, be resident in an ODA-eligible country and show a clear intention to support your country of award
Commit to returning to your home country (country of award) for at least two years after your scholarship ends
Have at least two years' work experience (2,800 hours) acquired after completing your undergraduate degree, spread over a minimum of two years
Hold an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme, completed at least two years before the application deadline (certificate needed by interview)
Apply to three different and eligible UK university courses and hold an unconditional offer from at least one by the deadline on the application timeline

SIDS applicants must study on courses that address a national development priority or capacity shortage: human rights, democracy and the rule of law; climate change and sustainability; economic recovery and growth; supportive societies that help people lead peaceful and productive lives
requirements: Apply for a Chevening Scholarship through the standard application process from your own country/territory page and opt in to be considered for the Chevening SIDS Scholarship

Complete the online application form in English and provide two referees; if shortlisted, upload photo ID, undergraduate degree certificate/diploma and two reference letters at least seven working days before the interview

Do not use AI-generated answers: 'The use of AI software to generate answers in Chevening applications is strictly prohibited' and Chevening uses tools to detect fraud, plagiarism and AI-generated text

Courses must be full-time, taught master's courses starting in the autumn term (usually September/October), based in the UK, lasting nine to 12 months, with no more than one month of study outside the UK; part-time, distance learning, PhD/DPhil and research-focused MRes programmes are not eligible
Applying is free: 'You do not need to pay anyone to apply, and Chevening does not endorse or work with third parties who charge for application support or advice'
documents: Undergraduate education certificate/diploma (official degree certificate - undergraduate transcripts are not accepted; original documents do not need translation)
Two reference letters from your nominated referees, in English
Unconditional offer letter from at least one of your three chosen UK courses (after a successful interview, by the offer deadline)
Conditional/Final Award Letter and Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) are issued before the scholar applies for a student visa
selection_criteria: Good examples of leadership and influencing skills
Good examples of building professional relationships to achieve positive outcomes
How the chosen course gives the skills to address pressing challenges linked to UK priority areas
How the career plan supports ambitions to drive positive change in the home country
Interview by a panel at a British embassy or high commission for shortlisted candidates
coverage: A monthly personal living allowance (stipend) to cover accommodation and living expenses (rate depends on studying inside or outside London)
Economy travel to and from your country of residence by an approved route for you only
The cost of an entry clearance (visa) application for you only
An arrival allowance, a departure allowance, a travel top up allowance, and up to £75 towards TB testing where required
For SIDS scholars: an enhanced UK programme of exclusive events and networking opportunities
application_method: Check eligibility against Chevening's published criteria and confirm your country is a participating SIDS country on the map
Register via the apply link on your country/territory page on chevening.org, consenting to terms and conditions
Pass the online eligibility checker and keep your unique access code
Complete each section of the online form (personal, immigration, education, work history, three UK master's course choices, essay answers)
Opt in to be considered for the Chevening SIDS Scholarship and submit; sift against eligibility criteria runs from October 2026
If shortlisted, upload photo ID, degree certificate and reference letters at least seven working days before the interview
Attend an interview at a British embassy or high commission (March to April 2027 for the last cycle)
If successful, submit at least one unconditional UK university offer by 17:00 BST on 8 July 2027
official.application_route: Apply for a standard Chevening Scholarship through the online system reached from your own country/territory page and opt in to the SIDS consideration within that application.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizen of one of the participating Small Island Developing States shown on the map on the SIDS page, meeting the standard Chevening rules: ODA residency if applying from an ODA-eligible country, and not resident in the UK at the time of application.
official.international_eligibility: Open to citizens of participating SIDS countries and territories worldwide; standard Chevening rules exclude UK residents at the time of application, British or dual British citizens (with limited exceptions), and recent employees of the FCDO, British Council, partner universities and their relatives.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Courses must address a national development priority or capacity shortage in one of four published areas: human rights, democracy and the rule of law; climate change and sustainability; economic recovery and growth; supportive societies that help people lead peaceful and productive lives.
official.duration: One-year master's degree in the UK; eligible courses last nine to 12 months
official.description: The Chevening SIDS Scholarship is an opportunity for outstanding individuals from Small Island Developing States to pursue a one-year master's degree in the UK, applying for all the standard benefits of the UK government's Chevening Scholarship programme with an additional enhanced UK programme of exclusive events and networking.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office)
official.english_requirement: No English test score is required by Chevening: 'While Chevening does not require you to submit an English language score as part of your application, many UK universities do.' No IELTS/TOEFL score is published by Chevening; strong English is needed to write the application, interview and study.

not_confirmed: participating SIDS country list (published only as an interactive map on the official page)
verification.notes: All facts verified live on chevening.org on 10 October 2026. Chevening publishes no monetary stipend figure on any official page: the FAQ states 'Your Conditional Award Letter will indicate your monthly stipend rate' and the Final Award Letter confirms it, so the amount, currency and period are recorded as null.

applicant_utility.summary: The SIDS award is not a separate application - you submit the standard Chevening application through your country/territory page and opt in for SIDS consideration, which Chevening says does not affect your chances of a standard scholarship. The money follows standard Chevening terms: tuition is paid and you receive a monthly stipend whose rate you only learn from your Conditional/Final Award Letter, so plan your budget against real UK living costs rather than any published figure. The 2027/28 round closed on 6 October 2026, so the realistic next shot is the round that opens around August 2027 for 2028 study - watch chevening.org and your country page from midsummer. Only pick courses that clearly address one of the four named development-priority areas, because that is an explicit SIDS requirement.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Citizens of participating Small Island Developing States who have already finished their undergraduate degree, can document at least 2,800 hours of post-degree work, can commit to two years back home, and can name three UK taught master's courses tied to the four published development-priority themes.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country appears on the participating-countries map on the SIDS page before investing any effort
Map your 2,800+ hours across up to fifteen employment entries in the form, making sure the experience spans at least two years

Use the Chevening course finder to pick three different eligible full-time taught master's courses starting September/October and lasting nine to 12 months, each linked to a named development-priority area
Brief your two referees early and make sure they can write in English and upload by the seven-working-day pre-interview deadline
Write the four essay areas in your own words - leadership and influencing, relationship-building, course fit with UK priority areas, and a realistic career plan - and avoid any AI assistance
Once the round opens, register from your country page, keep your unique access code safe, and submit well before 11:00 UTC on your country's deadline
Start chasing the unconditional offer with your universities as soon as applications open, because the offer deadline sits about nine months before study begins
common_rejection_risks: Being resident in the UK at the time of application, or holding British or dual British citizenship (with only narrow exceptions)
Having completed the undergraduate degree less than two years before the application deadline
Falling short of 2,800 hours, or cramming the hours into a period shorter than two years
Choosing ineligible courses: part-time, distance learning, PhD/DPhil, research-focused MRes, or more than one month of study outside the UK
AI-generated essay answers - Chevening runs detection tools and treats this as fraud
Missing the seven-working-day document upload deadline before the interview, which ends the application
Failing to secure and upload an unconditional offer from one of the three courses by the offer deadline
For SIDS applicants specifically: opting in but then choosing courses that do not address a national development priority or capacity shortage
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is published as covering basic living costs only - Chevening explicitly tells scholars to use it for NHS prescription, dental and optician charges - and it does not cover graduation travel, extra baggage beyond the departure allowance, transit visas, dependants' costs, or anything beyond the course. MBA students must personally cover any tuition above the £22,000 fee cap, and some universities require deposits that Chevening will not pay.
document_audit: The undergraduate certificate must be the official degree certificate - transcripts are explicitly not accepted - and you need the original in hand by interview time even if you applied before receiving it
Reference letters come from the two referees you nominate in the form, must be in English, and share the same seven-working-day pre-interview deadline as your degree certificate and photo ID
Photo ID is part of the interview-stage document upload, so a passport with limited validity is a real hazard
No translation is required for original degree documents
alerts: The 2027/28 cycle is closed as of 10 October 2026; nothing can be submitted until the next round opens (historically early August, with closure in early October)
Opting into the SIDS consideration does not improve or damage your standard Chevening chances - it only adds the enhanced programme if you win
SIDS scholars must study on a course addressing a national development priority or capacity shortage in the four named areas
You must return to your country of award for at least two years after the scholarship ends
Applications are free and Chevening does not endorse paid advisers or agents
Some country deadlines differed (20 October 2026 rather than 6 October) - always read your own country/territory page, not a summary
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register from your country/territory page, pass the eligibility checker, complete the online form with three course choices and the four essays, tick the SIDS opt-in, and submit before 11:00 UTC on your country's deadline; shortlisted candidates then upload documents at least seven working days before their embassy or high commission interview, and successful candidates upload an unconditional offer by the July offer deadline.

official.application_cycle: January 2027 entry (application form titled 'Postgraduate Sanctuary Scholarship 2026/27')
official.status_note: Open for applications for the January 2027 intake; the University publishes that all applicants will be informed of the outcome within two weeks after the deadline.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official page: 'Full tuition fee waiver and £1000/month for up to 12 months'; application form: 'It covers full tuition costs, plus a maintenance grant of £1,000 per month for 12 months'; central scholarship listing: 'Full tuition fee plus up to £12,000'.
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver for a full-time master's course starting January 2027
Maintenance grant of £1,000 per month for up to 12 months (headlined by the University as 'Full tuition fee plus up to £12,000')
eligibility: You must have an offer from the University of Westminster for a place on a full-time master's course starting in January 2027 (the form requires a conditional or unconditional offer in place before you apply)
You must be resident in the UK

You must hold one of the following eligible immigration statuses before submitting your application: UK asylum seeker; UK discretionary leave to remain (as a result of an asylum application); UK limited leave to remain (as a result of an asylum application)
Students who already have a master's degree are not eligible to apply
Students who are able to receive taught postgraduate student loans from Student Finance are not eligible to apply

The following categories of students are not eligible: Postgraduate Diploma; professional courses (eg RIBA pt III, ACCA, CIMA, CiLEX); conversion courses (eg Graduate Diploma in Law); integrated masters/MPhil/PhD; part-time students
requirements: Return your completed application form including required evidence as pdf attachments to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk
Submit everything in ONE email including your application and all relevant documents - you will not be able to amend your application once received
Have a conditional or unconditional offer from the University of Westminster in place before applying for the scholarship

Complete the form's personal details (including your 8-digit Westminster reference number from your offer letter), academic qualifications, professional experience and a personal statement of no more than 300 words
Sign the declaration confirming the information and documentary evidence supplied are accurate
documents: Completed Postgraduate Sanctuary Scholarship application form (PDF from the scholarship page)
Home Office letter confirming immigration status
Supporting statement/letter from an eligible referee (eg a teacher or a support worker from a charity like the Refugee Council)
selection_criteria: All eligible applications are considered by an awarding panel
The panel gives equal consideration to the applicant's academic record, personal circumstances and their answers to the questions posed in the application form
Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee an award - scholarships are limited
coverage: Full tuition costs for a full-time master's course starting January 2027
Maintenance grant of £1,000 per month for up to 12 months
application_method: Secure a conditional or unconditional offer for a full-time master's course at the University of Westminster starting January 2027
Download the Sanctuary Scholarship application form (PDF) from the official scholarship page

Complete the form, including the 300-word personal statement covering your migration circumstances, living conditions, immigration status, difficulties paying for education and living costs, and your motivation for the course or career goals
Gather the required evidence: Home Office letter confirming immigration status, Application registration card (asylum), and a supporting statement/letter from an eligible referee
Email the completed form with all evidence as PDF attachments to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk in a single email by 5pm on Monday 2 November 2026
official.application_route: Email the completed application form and all required evidence as PDF attachments in ONE email to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk by 5pm on Monday 2 November 2026, after securing a Westminster offer for a January 2027 full-time master's course.
official.citizenship_residency: You must be resident in the UK and hold, before applying, UK asylum seeker status, or UK discretionary or limited leave to remain as a result of an asylum application.
official.international_eligibility: Not open to overseas applicants - residence in the UK and an eligible asylum-related immigration status are mandatory; it supports students seeking asylum who are living in the United Kingdom.
official.duration: Full-time master's course starting January 2027; maintenance grant paid monthly for up to 12 months
official.description: The University of Westminster offers two Postgraduate Sanctuary Scholarships to support students who are seeking asylum and are living in the United Kingdom, covering full tuition costs plus a maintenance grant of £1,000 per month for up to 12 months.

not_confirmed: what happens to the award if the course is deferred
verification.notes: Amount, eligibility, deadline, required evidence and selection process verified live on westminster.ac.uk on 10 October 2026, cross-checked between the scholarship page, the central scholarships listing and the official application form PDF. No English language requirement, travel support or renewal provision is published on any official page.

applicant_utility.summary: Two Postgraduate Sanctuary Scholarships are on offer for January 2027 entry, each worth full tuition plus £1,000 per month for up to 12 months (the University headlines this as 'full tuition fee plus up to £12,000'), with applications due by 5pm on Monday 2 November 2026. You must already hold a Westminster offer - conditional or unconditional - before you can apply, and the entire application, including evidence, must go in a single email to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk. An awarding panel weighs your academic record, personal circumstances and form answers equally, and everyone hears the outcome within two weeks of the deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: People who are seeking asylum in the UK, or hold discretionary or limited leave to remain following an asylum application, who already hold (or can quickly secure) an offer for a full-time Westminster master's starting January 2027 and cannot access taught postgraduate student loans.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for and secure your Westminster offer first - the form is explicit that you need a conditional or unconditional offer in place before applying, and you will need your 8-digit Westminster reference number from the offer letter

Check your course is not in an excluded category: Postgraduate Diploma, professional courses (RIBA pt III, ACCA, CIMA, CiLEX), conversion courses (Graduate Diploma in Law), integrated masters/MPhil/PhD, or part-time study
Locate your Home Office letter confirming immigration status and your asylum Application registration card - both are mandatory evidence
Ask a teacher, support worker or charity support worker (for example from the Refugee Council) early for the supporting statement, since it is a required document

Draft the personal statement within the 300-word limit, covering the circumstances that led you to migrate, how long you have lived in the UK, your living conditions, your immigration status and the difficulties you face paying for education and living costs
Assemble the form and all evidence as PDF attachments and send them in ONE email before 5pm on Monday 2 November 2026 - there is no chance to correct or add anything afterwards
common_rejection_risks: Applying before holding a Westminster offer - the form states you need one in place before you can apply
Already holding a master's degree, which is an explicit exclusion
Being able to receive taught postgraduate student loans from Student Finance, which also disqualifies you
Being on an excluded course type (PG Dip, professional, conversion, integrated masters/MPhil/PhD, part-time) rather than a full-time master's
Failing to evidence immigration status with both the Home Office letter and the asylum registration card
Sending documents in a follow-up email or asking to amend the application - only one email is accepted and no changes are possible after receipt
Missing the 5pm cut-off on Monday 2 November 2026
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Beyond full tuition and the £1,000 monthly grant there is no published travel or visa support (unsurprising for UK-resident students), and dependants' costs, general London living expenses beyond the grant, course materials and any second year are for the student to fund. Note the form's warning that once you are awarded a Home Office status that gives you access to student finance, you will not receive any outstanding maintenance payment.
document_audit: Two separate Home Office documents are required - the letter confirming immigration status AND the asylum application registration card; one alone is not enough

The supporting statement must come from an eligible referee such as a teacher or a support worker from a charity like the Refugee Council - a statement from a family member will not meet the published wording
Everything must be attached as PDFs to the first and only email; sending files in the wrong format or splitting them across emails breaks the process
The declaration you sign makes accuracy legally significant: information later found to be incorrect or untrue can result in the scholarship being withdrawn
alerts: One email only, and no amendments once the University has received your application
You must hold a conditional or unconditional Westminster offer BEFORE applying for the scholarship
The award is tied to a full-time master's course starting January 2027 - it cannot be moved to a later intake on the published terms
Only two awards exist, so meeting the eligibility criteria is not enough on its own
Outcomes are issued within two weeks of the 2 November 2026 deadline, so plan any funding alternatives around late November
Westminster runs a separate one-place Sanctuary Scholarship for students with Indefinite Leave to Remain or Discretionary Leave to Remain - a different award with its own rules
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure your Westminster offer for January 2027, download and complete the application form from the scholarship page, attach your Home Office letter, asylum registration card and referee statement as PDFs, and email everything in one message to scholarships@westminster.ac.uk before 5pm on Monday 2 November 2026; the awarding panel then informs all applicants of the outcome within two weeks of the deadline.
